name: Temporary tattoos for cosplay markings

lead: Temporary tattoos for cosplay are removable designs, usually decal transfers or body paint, applied to the skin to reproduce markings seen on fictional characters. They let a person match a character's look for a convention or shoot and remove the design afterwards.
The appeal is that the character's markings can be added or changed without the permanence of a tattoo, which places pigment in the dermis and remains for years [1].

paras: Cosplayers apply a printed transfer or draw the design with skin-safe paint, usually just before the event, and remove it with the cleanser or oil the product recommends. Designs can be layered with makeup to blend them into the costume.
Possible skin irritation or allergic reaction to adhesives or pigments, particularly on sensitive skin. Product instructions typically recommend checking ingredients and testing a small area first.

angle.text: The design sits on the skin and gives an immediate, visible match to a character's markings. It is used for events and photo shoots and can be removed afterwards.

lead: Temporary tattoos for cosplay markings are removable designs applied to the skin to copy tattoos, scars, symbols or other body markings from fictional characters. They are used so a costume matches the source material in detail without a permanent change to the body.

Unlike a conventional tattoo, in which pigment is placed in the dermis and the body's immune cells gradually move the particles into deeper layers,[1] temporary versions stay on the surface and wash or wear off. Common forms are decal transfers, airbrush stencils and paint, which are among the temporary types listed in general references on tattoos.[1]
Published research specific to cosplay use has not been found; the technique is documented through product and community practice.

Permanent tattoo pigment lies in the dermis

paras: Temporary designs are applied to the surface of the skin, and general references on tattooing list decal, airbrush and henna types among temporary options.[1]
Cosplayers choose them to reproduce markings such as arm sleeves, face marks or symbols, and often blend them with makeup.
Permanent tattooing uses needles to place pigment into the dermis, and regulators in many countries oversee it because of infection and virus-transmission risks.[1] Temporary options avoid needles.
